get.description:
Authenticated reachability check: a 200 confirms the filter is up and the
caller's token is valid. `data.instance` is `"filter"` so the frontend can tell
which kind of node it reached (same shape as the controller's `/auth/ping`).

delete.description:
Removes `EvaluationRecord`s from the database `records` table having a timestamp less than the given parameter `prune_threshold_ts`.
Should be used periodically once records have been transferred out of the filter's database.

Returns the full publish history for the port (newest first). Each entry
carries the full `RuleSetRaw` for that revision, so the caller can replay any
past ruleset by re-publishing it via PUT /ports/{port}/ruleset (rollback).

Takes a `RuleSetRaw`, validates it, and returns the validation output, withouth changing the runtime configuration.
Useful for dry-runs / pre-validation

Per-port statistics are not collected yet. This endpoint only validates the
port (404 if unknown) and reports that stats are disabled; it is a
placeholder for future counters.

Returns this filter's version string and a snapshot of its effective runtime
config (upstream host, port bindings, control bind, limits, db path) so the

AuthPingData.description:
Response `data` for `/auth/ping` on **both** the filter and the controller.

`/auth/ping` is the authenticated reachability check the web UI uses: a 200
confirms the node is up *and* the caller's token is valid. `instance` tells
the frontend which kind of node answered without needing a separate call.

instance.description: Which kind of node answered: `"filter"` or `"controller"`.

CmpOp.description:
Comparison operator used by numeric matchers (`size`, `session.lifetime`,
`session.idle`). Serialized as its symbol (`"<"`, `">="`, …) so existing
rulesets keep working, and parsed exactly once at deserialization time.

PortChannel.description:
Transport channel a guarded service speaks on a given public port.

Immutable: it is fixed at filter configuration time. A port is `Tls` when it
has a certificate and key configured (`TLS_MAP`), in which case the filter
terminates client TLS and re-encrypts to the upstream; otherwise it is plain
`Tcp`. Surfaced in [`PortInfo`](crate::types::ruleset_types::PortInfo) so the
UI can show the division at a glance.

channel.description:
Transport channel (immutable): `tcp` for cleartext, `tls` for a
TLS-terminated+re-encrypted port. Derived from the port's certificate
configuration at filter startup.

enabled_scopes.description: List of scopes that are enabled for this port

hex_color.description: Optional hex color code (e.g. `"#ff00ff"`) used for UI indicators

name.description: Optional human-readable name for this port mapping

public.description: The public-facing port number that clients connect to

upstream.description: The internal/upstream port number to which traffic is forwarded

PortSnapshot.description: Complete, transferrable port information (includes `PortInfo`, `RuleSetRaw` and version).

ver_info.description: Version for `PortInfo` (hash of all its fields)

ver_ruleset.description: Version for `RuleSetRaw` (hash of all its fields)

Protocol.description:
Wire protocol detected for a single evaluated message.

`http/*` are framed HTTP messages; only 1.0 and 1.1 are parsed. HTTP/2 is
detected from its connection preface and tagged but not parsed (its fields are
not extracted, and stream matchers still see the raw bytes). `raw-*` are
unframed stream chunks, split by whether the bytes look like text (`raw-ascii`,
for example a CLI or TUI protocol) or not (`raw-binary`, unknown binary
protocols). Detection is best-effort and per-message.

commit_message.description: Optional git-style commit message describing this ruleset revision.

RulesetHistoryEntry.description: One historical ruleset revision for a port.

ruleset.description:
The full ruleset for this revision; its commit message is
`ruleset.commit_message`. Rollback is a plain re-publish of this value.

updated_at_ns.description: Wall-clock time this revision was published, in nanoseconds.

version.description:
Content-hash version of this revision (markers + filters only, so a
rollback to identical content shares the version of the revision it
restores; a commit-message-only change keeps the same version too).
